    """The reads of the facts a seed of `call` carries (`./history` reads them
    the same way for the seed): the facts of the last seed or feed of the
    call, the notes, the newest inner turns and the newest named topic of the
    round, the screen topics."""
    st_keys = [SEED_FACTS_KEY + call, SCREEN_KEY]
    topic_cols = ["seq", "session_id", "value", "audience_set"]
    if TOPIC_AGING:
        # GH #1436: the topic aged as the seed ages it -- the call's opening,
        # the naming mark's turn and (below) the person's rows that count the
        # turns. Off, the reads as before.
        st_keys.append(CALL_OPENED_KEY + call)
        topic_cols = ["seq", "session_id", "turn_id", "value", "audience_set"]
    ops = [("l-st", sel("state", ["key", "value"], {"key": {"in": st_keys}})),
           ("l-notes", round_sel("notes", NOTE_READ_COLS, None, the_round, None)),
           ("l-inner", round_sel("wall", ["seq", "session_id", "turn_id", "kind",
                                          "audience_set"],
                                 {"kind": {"in": INNER_KINDS}},
                                 the_round, session, [("seq", "desc")], INNER_READ)),
           ("l-topic", round_sel("marks", topic_cols,
                                 {"kind": "topic", "value": {"neq": NOTHING_TOPIC}},
                                 the_round, session, [("seq", "desc")], 1))]
    if TOPIC_AGING:
        ops.append(("l-age", round_sel("wall", ["seq", "session_id", "turn_id", "audience_set"],
                                       {"kind": "user"}, the_round, session,
                                       [("seq", "desc")], TOPIC_AGE_ROWS)))
    if WELLBEING_LINE:
        # D38 V2 (GH #1451, T-7): the day's facts and the wellbeing marks that
        # closed one, as the seed reads them -- the feed's state is the seed's.
        ops.append(("l-well", round_sel("marks", ["seq", "session_id", "kind", "value", "at",
                                                  "audience_set"],
                                        {"kind": {"in": ["fact", "wellbeing"]},
                                         "seq": {"gte": wellbeing_day()[1]}},
                                        the_round, session, [("seq", "desc")], WELLBEING_ROWS)))
    return [(cid, a) for cid, a in ops if a is not None]


def live_change(lg_, session, last, call=""):
    """`(state, change)`: the facts a seed of the call carries as they stand
    now (`seed_fact_state`) and what of them is new against `last` (the
    state of the call's last seed or feed, {} for none) -- one source with
    the seed: what is fed is what the next seed says."""
    st = state_of(lg_, "l-st")
    l_notes = [r for r in rows(lg_, "l-notes") if allowed(the_round, r.get("audience_set"))]
    # Review o15-Rv1 m2: the seed's notes, one per item with the knob.
    notes = seed_notes(rows_latest_per_item(l_notes) if NOTES_PER_ITEM else l_notes, now_ms())
    inner = [r for r in rows(lg_, "l-inner") if passes(r, the_round, session)]
    inner_seq = max([int(r.get("seq") or 0) for r in inner] or [0])
    named = [r for r in rows(lg_, "l-topic") if passes(r, the_round, session)]
    topic = topic_now(named)
    if TOPIC_AGING and "l-age" in lg_:
        # GH #1436: aged as the seed ages it (`topic_aged`); the closed turn's
        # session asks, the call's opening as the opening seed wrote it.
        aged = rows(lg_, "l-age")
        topic = topic_aged(topic, named[0] if named else None,
                           [r for r in aged if passes(r, the_round, session)], session,
                           call_opened_of(st.get(CALL_OPENED_KEY + call, "")),
                           len(aged) >= TOPIC_AGE_ROWS)
    screen_raw = st.get(SCREEN_KEY, "")
    state = seed_fact_state(notes, inner_seq, topic, screen_raw)
    if WELLBEING_LINE:
        # D38 V2 (GH #1451): the open wellbeing as the seed carries it, the
        # day in UTC (`YYYY-MM-DD`, the seed's clock `wellbeing_day`) -- one
        # digest with the seed's: the call's own closing mark does not close
        # it for the call (review o15-Rv1 I1).
        state = with_wellbeing(state, wellbeing_line(
            [r for r in rows(lg_, "l-well") if passes(r, the_round, session)],
            wellbeing_day()[0], call))
    if last.get("digest") == state["digest"]:
        return state, {}
    change = {}
    seen = set(last.get("notes") or [])
    new_notes = [{"source": n["source"], "id": n["id"], "text": n["text"]} for n in notes
                 if "%s:%s" % (n["source"], n["id"]) not in seen]
    if new_notes:
        change["notes"] = new_notes
    since = int(last.get("inner_seq") or 0)
    new_inner = [{"turn_id": str(r.get("turn_id") or ""), "kind": str(r.get("kind") or "")}
                 for r in sorted(inner, key=lambda r: int(r.get("seq") or 0))
                 if int(r.get("seq") or 0) > since]
    if new_inner:
        change["inner_turns"] = new_inner
    if topic != str(last.get("topic") or ""):
        change["topic"] = topic
    if state["screen"] != str(last.get("screen") or ""):
        names = loads(screen_raw, [])
        change["screen_topics"] = [str(t.get("name") or "") for t in names
                                   if isinstance(t, dict)] if isinstance(names, list) else []
    if not change:
        # The digest moved by what no field says (a note gone, an inner turn
        # dropped out of the gate): the seed differs, the feed says so.
        change["notes"] = []
    return state, change


def topic_of(value):
    """(movement, name) of one `topic` mark in the form OR-KY-71 writes --
    canonical JSON `{"movement": .., "name": ..}`, `name` empty when the memory
    section named none -- or None for any other value."""
    try:
        v = json.loads(str(value or ""))
    except Exception:
        return None
    if not isinstance(v, dict):
        return None
    movement = str(v.get("movement") or "").strip().lower()
    if movement not in MOVES:
        return None
    return movement, str(v.get("name") or "").strip()


def topic_now(marks):
    """`judge.topic`: the name of the newest named `topic` mark, "" when it
    ended the topic or there is none."""
    for m in marks:
        t = topic_of(m.get("value"))
        if t is not None:
            return "" if t[0] == "end" else t[1]
    return ""


def wellbeing_line(marks, day, call=""):
    """D38 V2 (GH #1451, T-7): the day's open wellbeing as ONE line of data,
    or None. ONE rule in two cells, this text byte for byte in `./history`
    (the seed a call starts with) and `./policy` (the live feed of a call),
    as `topic_aged`. `marks` are `fact` and `wellbeing` marks in any order,
    `day` the UTC day (`YYYY-MM-DD`) the asking call `call` speaks in. The newest
    `fact` mark of `day` with the class `wellbeing: true` (the model set it on
    the fact, the intake kept it), at a confidence of at least
    `wellbeing_min_confidence` (a mark without one passes: the intake marks
    checked items only) is
    `{state: "open", subject, predicate, claim, fact_seq}`. A `wellbeing`
    mark `{state: "closed", fact_seq}` -- booked by the seed that carried the
    line -- closes it: asked after once, then followed. The mark of the
    asking call itself (`session_id` == `call`) does not close it for that
    call: its seed carried the line, so its live feed carries it on and the
    digest stays the seed's (review o15-Rv1 I1); every later call is closed.
    Another day, a closed fact, none, or off (`wellbeing_line` "0"): None.
    Data, never prose: the words belong to the model (R-TR-27).
    GH #1456 (D58 F1, analysis section 2): the line keyed on the predicate
    `health` or `needs`/`unfulfilled`; the sidecar writes predicates as open
    keys (has_symptom, reports_symptom, health_status, ...) and never wrote
    either, so both branches were dead. A predicate family here would be a
    word list; the model classifies the fact instead, closed, at the fact."""
    if not WELLBEING_LINE:
        return None
    closed, best = set(), None
    for m in marks or []:
        try:
            v = json.loads(str(m.get("value") or "") or "{}")
        except ValueError:
            continue
        if not isinstance(v, dict):
            continue
        if m.get("kind") == "wellbeing":
            if v.get("state") == "closed" and not (call and str(m.get("session_id") or "") == call):
                closed.add(int(v.get("fact_seq") or 0))
            continue
        if m.get("kind") != "fact" or str(m.get("at") or "")[:10] != str(day or ""):
            continue
        if v.get("wellbeing") is not True:
            continue
        try:
            conf = 1.0 if v.get("confidence") is None else float(v.get("confidence"))
        except (TypeError, ValueError):
            continue
        seq = int(m.get("seq") or 0)
        if conf >= WELLBEING_MIN_CONFIDENCE and (best is None or seq > best[0]):
            best = (seq, v)
    if best is None or best[0] in closed:
        return None
    return {"state": "open", "subject": str(best[1].get("subject") or ""),
            "predicate": str(best[1].get("predicate") or ""),
            "claim": str(best[1].get("claim") or ""), "fact_seq": best[0]}


def wellbeing_day():
    """D38 V2 (review o15-Rv1 m3): `(day, first_us)` -- the UTC day
    (`YYYY-MM-DD`) the open wellbeing is read for and its first microsecond
    (the marks' `seq`). ONE clock in `./history` (the seed) and `./policy`
    (the feed), this text byte for byte: the param `now_utc` (RFC 3339, the
    lab clock), else the wall clock -- a lab run sees one day in both."""
    t = None
    fixed = str(P.get("now_utc") or "").strip()
    if fixed:
        try:
            t = datetime.datetime.fromisoformat(fixed.replace("Z", "+00:00"))
            if t.tzinfo is None:
                t = t.replace(tzinfo=datetime.timezone.utc)
        except ValueError:
            t = None
    if t is None:
        # wall-clock: now_utc
        t = datetime.datetime.now(datetime.timezone.utc)
    t = t.astimezone(datetime.timezone.utc)
    d0 = datetime.datetime(t.year, t.month, t.day, tzinfo=datetime.timezone.utc)
    return d0.date().isoformat(), int(d0.timestamp()) * 1000000


def rows_latest_per_item(note_rows):
    """D38 V1 (review o15-Rv1 m2): the `notes` rows without the older of one
    `(source, item)` -- the youngest by `at`, then `note_id`, stands (the
    window's `latest_per_item`); a row without an item always stays. ONE
    text in `./history` (the seed) and `./policy` (the feed), behind the
    one knob `notes_latest_per_item`."""
    best = {}
    for r in note_rows:
        item = str(r.get("item") or "")
        if item:
            k = (str(r.get("source") or ""), item)
            rank = (str(r.get("at") or ""), str(r.get("note_id") or ""))
            if k not in best or rank > best[k][0]:
                best[k] = (rank, r)
    return [r for r in note_rows if not str(r.get("item") or "")
            or best[(str(r.get("source") or ""), str(r.get("item") or ""))][1] is r]


def with_wellbeing(state, line):
    """D38 V2 (GH #1451): a facts state of `seed_fact_state` that carries the
    open wellbeing `line` as data, the digest over it too -- ONE text in
    `./history` and `./policy` beside `seed_fact_state` (left as it was, its
    twin lock stays). `line` None: the state as it came, byte for byte."""
    if line is None:
        return state
    out = {k: v for k, v in state.items() if k != "digest"}
    out["wellbeing"] = line
    out["digest"] = hashlib.sha256(
        json.dumps(out, sort_keys=True).encode("utf-8")).hexdigest()[:16]
    return out


def topic_aged(topic, named, wall, session_now="", opened_seq=0, full=False):
    """GH #1436: `topic` as it frames the asking turn now. ONE rule in two
    cells, this text byte for byte in `./history` (the route stamp, the judge,
    the seed of a call) and `./policy` (the live feed of a call) -- two
    readers of one fact parted once (the feed fed back what the seed had aged
    out), `gh1436_d` holds the twins equal. `named` is the mark that last
    named the topic (`{seq, session_id, turn_id?}`), `wall` the person's rows
    of the read's scope (`kind` `user`, one per turn, newest first, through
    the gate, the running turn left out), `session_now` the asking session
    ("" = the session of the newest row of `wall`), `opened_seq` the seq the
    asking call opened at (0 = unknown), `full` the `wall` read came back
    with `topic_age_rows` rows. "" when the call opened after the naming,
    when the asking session is not the naming one, or once `topic_age_turns`
    turns stood after the naming -- turns, not marks: a tool round or an
    answer without its `memory` block leaves no mark and is a turn all the
    same. A full read that never reached the naming counts as the bound.
    Off (`topic_aging` "0"): `topic` as read."""
    if not TOPIC_AGING or not topic or named is None:
        return topic
    seq = int(named.get("seq") or 0)
    if opened_seq and seq < int(opened_seq):
        return ""
    sess = str(session_now or "") or (str(wall[0].get("session_id") or "") if wall else "")
    if sess and sess != str(named.get("session_id") or ""):
        return ""
    later = {(str(r.get("session_id") or ""), str(r.get("turn_id") or ""))
             for r in wall if int(r.get("seq") or 0) > seq}
    if named.get("turn_id"):
        later.discard((str(named.get("session_id") or ""), str(named.get("turn_id") or "")))
    if len(later) >= TOPIC_AGE_TURNS:
        return ""
    if full and not any(int(r.get("seq") or 0) <= seq for r in wall):
        return ""
    return topic


def call_opened_of(value):
    """GH #1436: the seq (epoch microseconds) a call opened at, out of its
    `call_opened:<call>` row (written by `./history` with the call's opening
    seed); "" or out of form = 0, unknown."""
    try:
        v = json.loads(str(value or "") or "{}")
        return int(v.get("seq") or 0) if isinstance(v, dict) else 0
    except (TypeError, ValueError):
        return 0


def seed_notes(note_rows, stamp_ms):
    """GH #1279: the notes a seed carries and a live feed watches -- the
    session and until notes among `note_rows` (already through the round's
    gate) with a text and an `until` not passed, oldest first; a turn note
    is its own turn's and never a fact of the call. The same text in
    `./history` (the seed) and `./policy` (the feed), pinned."""
    out = []
    for r in note_rows:
        text = str(r.get("text") or "")
        if not text.strip() or str(r.get("scope") or "") not in ("session", "until"):
            continue
        u = epoch_ms(r.get("until"))
        if str(r.get("until") or "").strip() and u is not None and u <= stamp_ms:
            continue
        out.append({"source": str(r.get("source") or ""), "id": str(r.get("note_id") or ""),
                    "text": text, "at": str(r.get("at") or "")})
    return sorted(out, key=lambda n: (n["at"], n["source"], n["id"]))


def seed_fact_state(notes, inner_seq, topic, screen_raw):
    """GH #1279: the facts of a seed as one comparable state -- the note
    ids, the newest inner turn, the topic and the screen topics as stored --
    and their digest. `./history` keeps the state of the seed it sent,
    `./policy` the state of the feed it sent, under the same key
    (`seed_facts:<call>`); a feed leaves only when the digest moved."""
    state = {"notes": sorted("%s:%s" % (n["source"], n["id"]) for n in notes),
             "inner_seq": int(inner_seq or 0), "topic": str(topic or ""),
             "screen": hashlib.sha256(str(screen_raw or "").encode("utf-8")).hexdigest()[:16]}
    state["digest"] = hashlib.sha256(
        json.dumps(state, sort_keys=True).encode("utf-8")).hexdigest()[:16]
    return state

# GH #1260 (OR-WG-13, B-L6): where a running lookup looks, by tool family --
# the bridge says it in its own words ("I'm checking the weather service").
# A family without a row is not named at all (`lookup_phrase`).
LOOKUP_PLACES = {"weather": "at the weather service", "web": "on the web"}


def running_tools(scope):
    """The tools the tool round can call, for its bridge: the round's
    `tool_scope.allow` without its hint-stage families (named, not callable).
    A family with a row in `LOOKUP_PLACES` stands once by its family name
    (`web_search`, `web_fetch` -> `web`); the stamp is no guide here -- the
    lab stamped its weather turns `web` (r026e, all eleven tool rounds)."""
    scope = scope if isinstance(scope, dict) else {}
    hint = names_list(scope.get("hint"))
    out = []
    for name in names_list(scope.get("allow")):
        if name in hint:
            continue
        fam = name.split("_")[0]
        key = fam if fam in LOOKUP_PLACES else name
        if key not in out:
            out.append(key)
    return out


def lookup_phrase(tools):
    """Where the running lookup looks, in words: `on the web and at the
    weather service`. Words, never a tool's code name: told "with your tool
    `weather`", the fast model wrote the call out (JSON, a code fence, a
    "Fetching ..." prefix) or spoke made-up weather in 14 of 30 probe bridges
    (BL6 arm A, by the probe's counting rule); the words held 0 of 30
    (arm B). So a family without a row in `LOOKUP_PLACES` is not named: it
    adds `in other places` beside named ones, and alone it leaves the place
    out -- the sentence then only says the lookup is running."""
    places = [LOOKUP_PLACES[n] for n in tools if n in LOOKUP_PLACES]
    if places and len(places) < len(tools):
        places.append("in other places")
    return " and ".join(places)


def bridge_window(way, msgs):
    """The window of a bridge: on a consult and on a tool round the person's
    own turn, nothing before it; research keeps the quick window, it goes
    on talking for minutes. GH #1260 fix round 1 (OR-WG-13): an earlier
    answer in the window is a pattern the fast model follows -- it answered
    the consult in the bridge itself (a plan, a table, pros and cons) in 3
    of 5 probe bridges as logged and 5 of 12 with a sharper instruction, and
    asked "how cold tonight in Berlin?" after two short answers it said the
    degrees in 7 of 20 (17 of 20 with this wording); with the person's turn
    alone 0 of 12 and 0 of 20, all tool rounds 0 of 30 (BL6 arm C2). One
    sentence that says the answer is coming needs nothing else. No text of
    the person in the window (an empty window, only pins, only answers): the
    window without its pins (delta review 2 of U, M1) -- a pin is never the
    only `{origin: user}` element of the bridge.

    The turn is every text of the person since the last message that is not
    theirs, in order: a request sent in two messages ("how cold tonight?" /
    "in Berlin") keeps both (fix-round review M1). A pin is never part of it
    (`is_pin`): with `broadcast_mode` tail it stands as `{origin: user}`
    where it arrived, behind the turn when it came after it, and taken for
    the turn it made the bridge lose the request (fix-round review I1)."""
    if way not in ("consult", "tool"):
        return msgs
    turn = []
    for el in reversed(msgs):
        if is_pin(el):
            continue
        if isinstance(el, dict) and el.get("type") == "text" and \
                el.get("origin") in ("user", "peer"):
            turn.append(el)
        elif turn:
            break
    if turn:
        return list(reversed(turn))
    return [el for el in msgs if not is_pin(el)]


def is_pin(el):
    """A pin standing as a message (`pin_split`'s tail): its text in
    `PIN_FRAME`, behind the short id the window may put first."""
    if not isinstance(el, dict) or el.get("type") != "text":
        return False
    text = str(el.get("text") or "")
    if text.startswith("[#") and "] " in text:
        text = text[text.index("] ") + 2:]
    return text.startswith(PIN_FRAME.split("%s")[0])


def bridge_text(way, tools=None):
    """The bridge instruction of a way (`consult`, `research`, or `tool`: the
    tool round of a simple turn, GH #1260); `tools` are the tool round's
    running tools (`running_tools`)."""
    # GH #1258: one class for both ways -- the voice is the one handling the
    # request for the person. Told only "the backend is working on this
    # request", it heard a foreign party and, 3.4 s into a consult that was
    # planning a trip, said in its own name it could not plan trips (T7 on a
    # lab colony); the turn had to take it back.
    voice = ("You are handling this request for the person right now; speak in your own "
             "voice as the one doing it, never refuse it and never say you cannot do "
             "something. ")
    # GH #1260 (B-L3): every bridge speaks before the answer exists -- the
    # fast model made weather up on the tool round (lab r026c, turn 9), and
    # on a consult or a research turn the same model would make the plan up,
    # which the backend's answer then contradicts in the same turn.
    no_content = ("You do not have the answer: state no facts, no numbers, no results, "
                  "no guesses and no forecasts, not even likely ones; do not answer the "
                  "request yet. ")
    # GH #1260 (OR-WG-13, B-L6): "never say you cannot do something" was not
    # enough -- the tool round's bridge said "I have no access to current
    # weather data" plus a question which day, while the `weather` call ran
    # beside it (lab r026e, turn 9, quick rowid 10176 -> member 10212). The
    # bridge did not know a tool was working for it: it is told now what
    # runs, and talk of missing access, abilities or limits is out on every
    # bridge, since on each the answer is still coming.
    no_denial = "Never speak of missing access, missing abilities or limits of any kind. "
    # A question back about the running request is out on every bridge too;
    # the tool round's one sentence asks nothing at all. A consult or a
    # research turn keeps the conversation going while it waits (R-TR-27,
    # research for minutes), so there only the request itself is off limits
    # -- a question about anything else stays the person's conversation.
    ask_nothing = "Ask the person nothing: the answer is on its way. "
    ask_not_this = "Ask nothing about this request itself: its answer is on its way. "
    if way == "tool":
        # GH #1260 (OR-WG-6): the call itself is required and says nothing (a
        # probe: 10 of 10 calls, 0 of 10 with a sentence beside them), so this
        # sentence is the one the person hears while the lookup runs. It must
        # not answer: the fast model made weather and opening hours up when
        # it spoke without the result (lab r026, turns 5 and 9).
        # GH #1260 (OR-WG-9, B-L3): "do not answer yet" was not enough -- the
        # bridge said "tomorrow cloudy, 30 % rain" before any lookup (lab
        # r026c, turn 9, a 2.9k-token window after a long earlier answer).
        # Only that it is being looked up, nothing of the content.
        running = lookup_phrase(tools or [])
        return voice + ("Your lookup is already running right now%s; it was started for "
                        "you, and its result follows in this turn. Say one short sentence "
                        "that bridges the wait, in your own words: only that you are "
                        "looking it up, one moment. " % ((", " + running) if running else "")
                        + no_denial + ask_nothing + no_content
                        + "Speak plainly: write no tool call, no JSON, no code and no command.")
    if way == "consult":
        return voice + ("The answer follows in this turn, within about %d seconds. Say one "
                        "short sentence that bridges the wait, in your own words: only that "
                        "you are on it and the answer is still coming. "
                        % max(1, int(round(wait_ms("consult") / 1000.0)))
                        + no_denial + ask_not_this + no_content + "Call no tool.")
    # GH #1260 fix round 1 (R-TR-27): research keeps the conversation going
    # for minutes, so it may ask -- but on another subject. Told only "ask
    # nothing about this request itself; anything else is fine", it asked
    # in 3 of 5 probe bridges what mattered to the person in the request
    # (which kind of travel, which detail of the care insurance); told to
    # go on with another subject, 0 of 10 and 0 of 5 (BL6 arms C1, C2).
    return voice + ("It is researched in the background; that takes about %d minutes, and "
                    "the result comes in a later turn. Tell the person so in your own words "
                    "and name the waiting time. Then keep the conversation going on another "
                    "subject -- how they are, or what else is on their mind -- never on this "
                    "request: ask nothing about it, not its details, not their wishes or "
                    "experiences with it, not what matters to them in it; the research has "
                    "what it needs. "
                    % max(1, int(round(wait_ms("research") / 60000.0)))
                    + no_denial + no_content + "Call no tool.")

def frame_slot(skeleton):
    """The FORM one section's body takes in the shape line (GH #799): `{...}`
    for an object, `[...]` for a list, `"..."` for a string, the literal for
    a number, a boolean or null -- the brackets a model has to write, never a
    second copy of the example."""
    if isinstance(skeleton, dict):
        return "{...}"
    if isinstance(skeleton, list):
        return "[...]"
    if isinstance(skeleton, str):
        return "\"...\""
    return json.dumps(skeleton, separators=(",", ":"), ensure_ascii=False)


def sidecar_frame(req, opt):
    """The frame of the block contract over the sections it holds (GH #606):
    the preamble, the whole-object shape, the obligation by name. `req` and
    `opt` are `(name, slot)` pairs, required and optional, in the order the
    sections stand. `collector/assemble` writes it over every offered
    section; `curator/policy` writes it anew over the sections it kept, so
    the frame never asks for a section the contract left out (GH #1085)."""
    def names(items):
        return ", ".join('"%s"' % n for n, _ in items)
    shape = "{" + ", ".join('"%s": %s' % (n, s) for n, s in req + opt) + "}"
    parts = [SIDECAR_PREAMBLE, shape]
    if req:
        line = ("%s %s written on EVERY turn, even the ones that changed nothing"
                % (names(req), "is" if len(req) == 1 else "are"))
        line += (", and when %s %s present too: an optional section never"
                 " replaces a required one."

                 if opt else "; leaving one out is a fault.")
        parts.append(line)
    if opt:
        parts.append("Write %s only when it applies; otherwise leave its key"
                     " out." % names(opt))
    return "\n".join(parts)

def canonical(value):
    """The one serialisation a block is hashed and stored in: keys sorted,
    UTF-8, no whitespace."""
    return json.dumps(value, sort_keys=True, separators=(",", ":"), ensure_ascii=False)


def block_hash(value):
    return hashlib.sha256(canonical(value).encode("utf-8")).hexdigest()


def block_span(text):
    """Where an answer's sidecar block stands: (start, end) or None.

    The boundary is the fence `talky/splitter` cuts (GH #379, #605): the
    ```sidecar fence, or the legacy ```memory fence, to the next closing fence
    or to the end of the text when the completion stopped inside the block.
    Measured, never parsed -- the sections inside are somebody else's business.
    """
    low = text.lower()
    for fence in ("```sidecar", "```memory"):
        at = low.find(fence)
        if at < 0:
            continue
        head = text.find("\n", at)
        close = text.find("```", head + 1) if head >= 0 else -1
        if head >= 0 and close >= 0:
            return at, close + 3
        return at, len(text)
    return None


def stripped_text(text):
    span = block_span(text)
    if span is None:
        return text
    return (text[:span[0]] + text[span[1]:]).strip()


def dropped_text(text, size):
    """An answer whose sidecar block is over its share of the window: the
    answer, and the mark where the block stood (R-IG-1)."""
    bare = stripped_text(text)
    mark = SIDECAR_DROPPED % size
    return (bare + "\n\n" + mark) if bare else mark


def element_of(row):
    """The element a wall row stands for: `element` when the caller has it,
    else the block body the ledger stored."""
    el = row.get("element")
    if isinstance(el, dict):
        return el
    try:
        el = json.loads(str(row.get("body") or ""))
    except Exception:
        return None
    return el if isinstance(el, dict) else None


def plan_cover(plan, cover_rows):
    """Where the window's wall starts: the cover of the current plan, or --
    in a ledger that has none yet -- the newest summary's `covers_to_seq`."""
    if isinstance(plan, dict) and plan.get("cover") is not None:
        try:
            return int(plan.get("cover") or 0)
        except (TypeError, ValueError):
            pass
    return int((cover_rows[0].get("covers_to_seq") or 0) if cover_rows else 0)


def short_id(h):
    return str(h or "")[:ID_HEX]


def norm_id(value):
    """A block id as a model writes it -- `#0123456789ab`, `[#0123...]`,
    bare -- as its 12 hex digits, or "" when it is none."""
    s = str(value or "").strip().strip("[]").strip().lstrip("#").strip().lower()
    s = s[:12]
    if len(s) != 12 or any(c not in "0123456789abcdef" for c in s):
        return ""
    return s


def epoch_ms(value):
    """A stamped time as epoch milliseconds: RFC 3339 text, or a number of
    seconds (milliseconds above 1e12). None when it reads as neither."""
    if isinstance(value, (int, float)) and not isinstance(value, bool):
        return int(value if value > 1e12 else value * 1000)
    s = str(value or "").strip()
    if not s:
        return None
    try:
        t = datetime.datetime.fromisoformat(s.replace("Z", "+00:00"))
    except ValueError:
        return None
    if t.tzinfo is None:
        t = t.replace(tzinfo=datetime.timezone.utc)
    return int(t.timestamp() * 1000)


def epoch_us(value):
    """A stored stamp as epoch microseconds -- the unit of `wall.seq`, so a
    pin that arrived between two rows stands between them."""
    s = str(value or "").strip()
    try:
        t = datetime.datetime.fromisoformat(s.replace("Z", "+00:00"))
    except ValueError:
        return None
    if t.tzinfo is None:
        t = t.replace(tzinfo=datetime.timezone.utc)
    delta = t - datetime.datetime(1970, 1, 1, tzinfo=datetime.timezone.utc)
    return (delta.days * 86400 + delta.seconds) * 1000000 + delta.microseconds


def prefixable(el):
    """What carries a short id and a one-line form: somebody else's words and
    a tool result (see ID_HEX)."""
    typ = el.get("type")
    return typ == "tool_result" or (typ == "text" and el.get("origin") in ("user", "peer"))


def first_line(text, cap):
    """The first non-empty line of `text`, at most `cap` characters of it --
    a pointer's preview; the form around it says the whole length."""
    for line in str(text or "").splitlines():
        line = line.strip()
        if line:
            return line if len(line) <= cap else line[:cap].rstrip()
    return ""

def recall_row(line):
    """True for a row of a recall result in the form the memory hive renders
    it (`render_payload_lines`, GH #281): a line at an indent of exactly two
    that is no parenthesised caveat. The document head, the section heads and
    the notes above them stand unindented, the caveats at two in parentheses,
    a reply under a fact at four -- review I-1 of GH #1430: hashing those
    made two results without a fact in common duplicates and counted seven
    rows for three (OR-d38-1.k3.12). The shape, never the words."""
    if not line.startswith("  ") or line[2:3] in ("", " ", "\t"):
        return False
    body = line.rstrip()
    return not (body[2:].startswith("(") and body.endswith(")"))

    """The canonical hashes of the rows (`recall_row`) of a recall result
    (class `dup_recall`, `recall_rows`): the row stripped, sha256 of its
    UTF-8, the first 16 hex -- a row is the same row by its bytes, never by
    resemblance."""
    return [hashlib.sha256(line.strip().encode("utf-8")).hexdigest()[:16]
            for line in str(text or "").splitlines() if recall_row(line)]

    result `text` is a quote `<who>: "<words>"` (or `"<words>"`) whose words,
    first to last quote mark, hash (`row_lines` form) to a raw element of the
    window in `wall_hashes`. No row, or one row without such a quote, is
    False: the block stays."""
    rows_ = [line.strip() for line in str(text or "").splitlines() if recall_row(line)]
    for row in rows_:
        a, b = row.find('"'), row.rfind('"')
        head = row[:a]
        if a < 0 or b <= a or (head and not head.endswith(": ")):
            return False
        h = hashlib.sha256(row[a + 1:b].strip().encode("utf-8")).hexdigest()[:16]
        if h not in wall_hashes:
            return False
    return bool(rows_)


def closed_round(turn, as_of_ms):
    """True for the turn of an inner round (`round_label`) whose deadline
    (`round_deadline`, the `until` of its `pending:delegation:` row) lies at
    or before `as_of_ms`: the errand is over (OR-d38-1.k3.2)."""
    deadline = round_deadline(turn)
    return bool(round_label(turn)) and 0 < deadline and as_of_ms is not None \
        and deadline <= int(as_of_ms)


def shrinkable(r, el):
    """What the window may show in its one-line form when a plan shrank it: a
    tool result that is no error (GH #1430 -- a plan from before may name one),
    or the scaffold of a closed delegation."""
    if el.get("type") == "tool_result":
        return not is_error_result(el.get("text"))
    return str(r.get("kind") or "") in SCAFFOLD_KINDS


def sent_chars(r, gone):
    """The characters a wall row is sent at (GH #1434, review M-2): a row
    whose short id is in `gone` (`gone_ids`: shrunk, released or expired by
    the plan, which `render` shows in its one-line form) at FORM_CHARS, a
    final answer `render` cuts at its sidecar block (`with_cut`) at the
    characters of the cut text, every other at its block's characters. The
    one row rule of the raw budget and the `curate` stamp (`raw_estimate`),
    the plan's `estimate` and the `gc` mark's `tool_share`; before, each of
    them spelled it out."""
    if short_id(r.get("hash")) in gone:
        return FORM_CHARS
    cut = r.get("cut_chars")
    return int(cut) if cut is not None else int(r.get("chars") or 0)


def gone_ids(rows, shrunk, released, as_of_ms, current=None):
    """The short ids of the rows a plan sends in a one-line form (GH #1434,
    review m-2): `shrunk`, `released`, and every row of `rows` whose transient
    block ran out at or before `as_of_ms` (`expired`; `render` shows it as
    `EXPIRED_FORM`). A row carries `valid_until` itself (a rebuild's
    enriched wall) or in its element (the wall of a call). The one set the
    raw budget, its cap at the aim, the plan's `estimate`, the `gc` mark and
    the `curate` stamp hand `sent_chars`; before, the budget and the stamp
    each built it and the estimate left the expired rows out (review I-1':
    the cap at the aim counted them at their form, the estimate whole, and a
    plan that fit as sent was said over the aim). `current`, the running
    round `(session_id, turn_id)`: `render` sends its rows whole (`key !=
    current`), so a row only of it is never in the set -- an expired or
    released row of the running round counted at its form and went out
    whole, and the budget filled older rounds on top of it (rest list of the
    review of GH #1434)."""
    out = set(shrunk or ()) | set(released or ())
    if as_of_ms is not None:
        for r in rows:
            if r.get("valid_until") is not None:
                el = r
            elif r.get("element") is not None or r.get("body") is not None:
                el = element_of(r)
            else:
                continue
            if expired(el, as_of_ms):
                out.add(short_id(r.get("hash")))
    if current is not None:
        mine, others = set(), set()
        for r in rows:
            key = (str(r.get("session_id") or ""), str(r.get("turn_id") or ""))
            (mine if key == current else others).add(short_id(r.get("hash")))
        out -= mine - others
    return out


def sidecar_cut(row, el, cap):
    """The text a final answer of the model is sent at when its sidecar block
    is over `cap` characters (`render`, GH #871, R-IG-1) and the size of the
    block, `(text, size)`; None when it goes whole (no cap, no block, another
    row). The one rule of `render` and of the rows the raw budget and the
    `curate` stamp measure (`with_cut`, GH #1434: they counted the whole
    block, and the stamp could pass the call's own projection)."""
    if cap is None or el is None:
        return None
    if str(row.get("kind") or "") != "assistant" or int(row.get("final") or 0) != 1:
        return None
    text = str(el.get("text") or "")
    span = block_span(text)
    if span is None or span[1] - span[0] <= cap:
        return None
    size = span[1] - span[0]
    return dropped_text(text, size), size


def with_cut(row, el, cap):
    """`row` with `cut_chars`, the characters `render` sends of its cut
    answer (`sidecar_cut`), when it cuts one; else `row` itself."""
    cut = sidecar_cut(row, el, cap)
    return dict(row, cut_chars=len(cut[0])) if cut is not None else row


def gc_figure(rows, cover, keep, gone, classes, total_chars):
    """The value of the `gc` mark of a plan (without its call): the counts per
    class, `tool_share` -- the characters of the tool results the window keeps
    above the cover (a one-line form at `FORM_CHARS`) over all the estimate
    counts --, and `recall_rows`, the rows of the newest recall result that
    stays raw (OR-d38-1.k3.6). `gone` is the plan's `gone_ids`."""
    tools, recall = 0, None
    keep = set(keep)
    out = set(gone)
    for r in rows:
        s = int(r["seq"])
        if s <= cover and s not in keep:
            continue
        if r.get("type") == "tool_result":
            tools += sent_chars(r, out)
            if r.get("recall") and short_id(r.get("hash")) not in out:
                recall = r
    share = round(min(1.0, float(tools) / total_chars), 4) if total_chars > 0 else 0.0
    return {"classes": dict((c, int(classes.get(c) or 0)) for c in GC_CLASSES),
            "tool_share": share,
            "recall_rows": len((recall or {}).get("lines") or [])}


def raw_estimate(rows, gone, rate):
    """Tokens of `rows` as the window sends them (GH #1434): a row whose short
    id is in `gone` (shrunk or released by the plan) at FORM_CHARS, every
    other at its block's characters, over `rate` -- the one figure the raw
    budget (`keep_recent_tokens`) fills and the `curate` stamp names
    (`raw_tokens`). Before, the budget counted the rows before the garbage
    collection (a knob of 20000 left about 11000 raw tokens in the window) and
    the stamp `estimate_tokens` of their elements (about 1.37x the budget)."""
    return sum(sent_chars(r, gone) for r in rows) / rate


# THE MODEL'S RELEASES PER AUDIENCE (GH #932, review I-1). A release or a pin
# the model says is a `marks` row of the round it was said in; a rebuild
# reads only the marks its own round may see. The plan keeps what each
# audience said last about a block -- `marks_on[id][audience] = [group_seq,
# rank, seq, kind]` -- so a mark is never lost when a rebuild of another
# round runs, and it shapes only the windows of rounds that may see it.
def round_canon(round_value):
    """The canonical round: `"[]"` for none -- what `marks_on` and
    `marks_to_by` are keyed by. (`round_key` until GH #943, which gave that
    name to the short key of the state.)"""
    return audience_of(round_value) or "[]"


def round_key(round_value):
    """The key a round's state is kept under (GH #943): the first 12 hex
    digits of the sha256 of its canonical form (`round_canon`). The same
    round in another order or with duplicates is the same key; a round
    nobody declared has the key of `[]`; `["*"]` is a round of its own. A
    hash and not the canonical text: a `state` key stays short and plain
    whatever the round names. `./intake` keeps the same formula (OR-BC.W.1)."""
    return hashlib.sha256(round_canon(round_value).encode("utf-8")).hexdigest()[:12]


# The key of the round this message serves (GH #943): the suffix of every
# state key that is kept per round. Here and not beside `the_round`, because
# `round_key` is defined only now; lower case for the same reason as
# `the_round` (the pure half is loaded with the upper-case constants only).
the_rk = round_key(the_round)


def rkey(name, rk=None):
    """A state key of one round (GH #943): `<name>:<rk>`, this message's
    round unless `rk` names another."""
    return "%s:%s" % (name, the_rk if rk is None else rk)


def newest_slots(rows):
    """One `slots` row per path, as a PURE function (GH #1225, K-4): the
    newest by `at`, on a tie the smallest `hash` -- an explicit order, since
    the store's select names none and `rowid` is not readable through it. A
    row without a readable `at` is the oldest. Paths keep the order of their
    first row. Why: `slots` had no key on `path`, and two writes in flight
    left copies of one path (the review measured 21 copies of one path in 4
    versions); every reader counted each -- the window estimate, the leaves
    sent and `call_blocks` 21 times."""
    best, order = {}, []
    for r in rows:
        path = str(r.get("path") or "")
        at = epoch_us(r.get("at"))
        rank = (at if at is not None else -1, str(r.get("hash") or ""))
        cur = best.get(path)
        if cur is None:
            order.append(path)
        elif not (rank[0] > cur[0][0] or (rank[0] == cur[0][0] and rank[1] < cur[0][1])):
            continue
        best[path] = (rank, r)
    return [best[p][1] for p in order]


def own_slots(rows, rk, newest=True):
    """The `slots` rows as the round `rk` sees them (GH #943, OR-BC.W.2), as a
    PURE function: the summary slot of a round is the row
    `history.summary:<rk>`, shown as the leaf `history.summary`; the slot of
    another round and a bare `history.summary` row (from before the rule, not
    moved) are left out; every other row stays as it is. Why: with one
    summary slot per hive, the rebuild of one round replaced or deleted the
    summary leaf of another. One row per path (`newest_slots`, GH #1225) --
    `newest=False` only for a read that fetches blocks and counts nothing
    (`win-hashes`: `./intake` hands its slot hashes on without `at`, and the
    block of the newest copy has to come along whichever copy that is)."""
    out = []
    for r in (newest_slots(rows) if newest else rows):
        path = str(r.get("path") or "")
        if path == SUMMARY_PATH:
            continue
        if path.startswith(SUMMARY_PATH + ":"):
            if path != SUMMARY_PATH + ":" + rk:
                continue
            r = dict(r, path=SUMMARY_PATH)
        out.append(r)
    return out


def prune_plans(reg, rk, now_ms_value, max_plans, idle_s):
    """The registry of a hive's round plans after a rebuild of the round
    `rk` (GH #943), as a PURE function: `reg` maps a round key to the epoch
    ms of its last rebuild. `rk` is stamped `now_ms_value`; every other round
    idle for more than `idle_s` seconds goes, and then, while more than
    `max_plans` are left, the oldest (the smallest stamp, on a tie the
    smallest key) -- never `rk` itself. Returns `(new_reg, dropped)`, the
    dropped keys sorted. Why: a plan per round is a state row per round, and
    rounds come and go; "used" is the last rebuild, since a window without
    one lives no longer than the provider's cache."""
    out = {}
    for k, t in (reg or {}).items():
        try:
            out[str(k)] = int(t)
        except (TypeError, ValueError):
            # A stamp nobody can read is as old as it gets.
            out[str(k)] = 0
    out[rk] = int(now_ms_value)
    dropped = [k for k, t in out.items()
               if k != rk and int(now_ms_value) - t > idle_s * 1000]
    for k in dropped:
        del out[k]
    while len(out) > max_plans:
        rest = sorted((t, k) for k, t in out.items() if k != rk)
        if not rest:
            break
        dropped.append(rest[0][1])
        del out[rest[0][1]]
    return out, sorted(dropped)


def mark_applies(rk, aud):
    """Whether what the audience `aud` said holds for the round `rk`: the
    gate (`allowed`); for a round-less round (`"[]"`) only a round-less or a
    `*` audience, as `passes` lets a round-less read see only those rows --
    `allowed` would let every declared audience hold for an empty round."""
    if rk == "[]":
        a = audience_of(aud)
        return a is not None and (a == "[]" or "*" in json.loads(a))
    return allowed(rk, aud)


def marks_on_of(prev):
    """The `marks_on` a plan carries, or -- for a plan from before it -- its
    `released` as said by everybody, before any mark of this plan."""
    prev = prev if isinstance(prev, dict) else {}
    if isinstance(prev.get("marks_on"), dict):
        return dict((str(i), dict(v)) for i, v in prev["marks_on"].items() if isinstance(v, dict))
    return dict((str(i), {"[\"*\"]": [0, 0, 0, "release"]}) for i in (prev.get("released") or []))


def released_in(marks_on, rk):
    """The ids released for the round `rk`: those whose newest entry that
    holds for `rk` is a release."""
    out = set()
    for i, by in (marks_on or {}).items():
        best = None
        for aud, entry in (by or {}).items():
            if isinstance(entry, list) and len(entry) == 4 and mark_applies(rk, aud) \
                    and (best is None or entry > best):
                best = entry
        if best is not None and best[3] == "release":
            out.add(i)
    return out


# THE PLAN OF BUILDING BLOCKS (GH #1448, D38 C2, R-38-4 Nr. 2). Stage 1 of the
# curator: the window is a list of blocks `{id, kind, prio, origin, tokens,
# audience, valid_until}` kept in the round's plan (`window_plan:<rk>`, the one
# plan form: `blocks` and `blocks_to` beside the rebuild's keys), written after
# each answer (`tap`) and by a rebuild; a turn appends its new blocks only.
# Model free: `tokens` is the neutral estimate (`estimate_tokens`, three bytes
# a token) -- never a catalog row's `chars_per_token`, never `input_soft`
# (stage 2 sizes per target model). `prio` comes from the knob `block_prio`
# (kind -> whole number, R-IG-1); a kind it does not name has its `default`.
BLOCK_PLAN_KEYS = ("blocks", "blocks_to")


def block_prio_table(raw):
    """`block_prio` as kind -> whole number, from a JSON text or an object; a
    value that is no whole number is left out."""
    v = raw
    if not isinstance(v, dict):
        try:
            v = json.loads(str(raw or ""))
        except ValueError:
            v = {}
    v = v if isinstance(v, dict) else {}
    return {str(k): x for k, x in v.items() if isinstance(x, int) and not isinstance(x, bool)}


BLOCK_PRIO = block_prio_table(P.get("block_prio"))


def prio_of(kind):
    return int(BLOCK_PRIO.get(kind, BLOCK_PRIO.get("default", 0)))


def rebuilt_part(plan):
    """The plan without its blocks: what a rebuild made (cover, keep, summary,
    ...). Every step that reads the rebuild's keys reads this, so a plan of
    blocks only reads as no plan -- the window of before, byte for byte."""
    plan = plan if isinstance(plan, dict) else {}
    return {k: v for k, v in plan.items() if k not in BLOCK_PLAN_KEYS}


# OR-d38-3.o10.2 (review I1): the pairs `./push` hands `./intake` -- a gap's
# find and the candidates -- are push lines, whatever their ledger kind.
PUSH_IDS = ("call_addendum_", "call_candidates_")


def block_kind(el, wall_kind=""):
    """The kind of the block of the wall element `el` (its ledger kind beside)."""
    t = str(el.get("type") or "")
    if t in ("tool_call", "tool_result") and str(el.get("id") or "").startswith(PUSH_IDS):
        return "push"
    if t == "tool_result":
        amb = ambient_of(el)
        if wall_kind == "recall" or amb == "recall":
            return "recall"
        return "brief" if amb == "brief" else "tool_result"
    if t == "tool_call":
        return "tool_call"
    if wall_kind in SCAFFOLD_KINDS:
        return "note"
    return "answer" if str(el.get("origin") or "") == "assistant" else "words"


def block_of(kind, el, origin, audience, valid_until=None):
    """One block: id `<kind>:<12 hex of its origin>` (OR-d38-3.c2.1)."""
    h = str(origin.get("hash") or "") or block_hash(origin)
    return {"id": "%s:%s" % (kind, short_id(h)), "kind": kind, "prio": prio_of(kind),
            "origin": origin, "tokens": int(estimate_tokens(el)), "audience": audience,
            "valid_until": valid_until}


def rebuild_blocks(plan, rows, blocks, audience):
    """GH #1448 (Z1.6): the blocks of the plan a rebuild made -- the wall rows
    its window still shows (over `cover`, or kept), a released, shortened or
    run-out one as a `stub`, in seq order; the condensate is `with_brief`'s."""
    cover = int(plan.get("cover") or 0)
    keep = set(int(x) for x in (plan.get("keep") or []) if str(x).lstrip("-").isdigit())
    released, shrunk = set(plan.get("released") or []), set(plan.get("shrunk") or [])
    out, seen = [], set()
    for r in sorted(rows, key=lambda r: int(r.get("seq") or 0)):
        seq, h = int(r.get("seq") or 0), str(r.get("hash") or "")
        el = element_of(blocks.get(h) or {})
        if el is None or (seq <= cover and seq not in keep):
            continue
        wid = short_id(h)
        # Z1.9: every class of the garbage collection marks its block -- a
        # released, a shortened and a run-out one (`transient`) is a stub.
        gone = wid in released or (wid in shrunk and shrinkable(r, el)) \
            or (seq > cover and expired(el, plan.get("as_of_ms")))
        kind = "stub" if gone else block_kind(el, str(r.get("kind") or ""))
        b = block_of(kind, el, {"source": "wall", "hash": h}, audience, el.get("valid_until"))
        if b["id"] not in seen:
            seen.add(b["id"])
            out.append(b)
    return out


def with_brief(plan, h, el, audience):
    """GH #1448 (Z1.6): the plan with its condensate as one `brief` block in
    front (origin the summary block `h`), none when the plan holds no
    summary; the brief of before goes."""
    rest = [b for b in plan.get("blocks") or []
            if (b.get("origin") or {}).get("source") != "summary"]
    if plan.get("summary") and h:
        rest = [block_of("brief", el or {}, {"source": "summary", "hash": h}, audience)] + rest
    return dict(plan, blocks=rest)


def blocks_of_rows(rows, have, audience):
    """The blocks of the wall rows `rows` (each with its `body` or element
    `el`), in their order, but for the ids in `have` (a row already planned)."""
    out, seen = [], set(have)
    for r in rows:
        el = r.get("el")
        if not isinstance(el, dict):
            el = element_of(r) or {}
        h = str(r.get("hash") or "") or block_hash(el)
        b = block_of(block_kind(el, str(r.get("kind") or "")), el,
                     {"source": "wall", "hash": h}, audience, el.get("valid_until"))
        if b["id"] not in seen:
            seen.add(b["id"])
            out.append(b)
    return out


def note_blocks(text, refs, audience):
    """OR-d38-3.o10.2 (review I1): the notes block `text` as blocks of the
    call -- each line of a note in `refs` (its order, `note_ref`s) one block,
    the state line `state`, every other `note`, origin the hash of the line.
    A note whose text holds a line break of the list form leaves the lines
    one `note` block; the text sent is never touched."""
    lines = text.split("\n- ")[1:] if text else []
    kinds = ["state" if r.get("source") == "curator" and r.get("id") == STATE_NOTE_ID
             else "note" for r in refs]
    if len(lines) != len(kinds):
        lines, kinds = (["\n- ".join(lines)], ["note"]) if lines else ([], [])
    out = []
    for kind, line in zip(kinds, lines):
        el = {"text": "- " + line}
        out.append(block_of(kind, el, {"source": "note", "hash": block_hash(el)}, audience))
    return out


def render(blocks, rows, params=None, plan=None, current=None, tail=None, round_value=None,
           cuts=None):
    """Every message of the window, in order: `(position, element, hash, view)`.

    GH #1448 (Z1.10): the window is its plan's `blocks` -- a wall row of
    `rows` (the bodies) is rendered when a block of the wall names its hash,
    never because the wall holds it; a row twice of one content (one block
    id, OR-d38-3.c2.7) comes twice, as the wall has it.

    Four rules, all deterministic in their input:
    * a final answer of the model shows its sidecar block whole, unless the
      window is known (`params["input_soft"]`, tokens) and the block is over
      its share of it (`SIDECAR_SHARE`); then the answer shows the mark
      `SIDECAR_DROPPED` where the block stood (GH #871: without a precedent
      in the earlier answers the block quote fell from 98 % to 38 %; R-IG-1:
      what is left out is said, never silent);
    * a tool call without its result, or a result without its call, in the same
      turn is left out -- a malformed pair is a refused request for every
      provider;
    * outside the running round (`current`, one `(session_id, turn_id)`), a
      block the plan released, shrank or found expired is shown in its one-line
      form (GH #892);
    * with short ids on, somebody else's words and a tool result begin with
      `[#<12 hex>] `, the id of the wall block (GH #892).
    `view` is true where the element differs from the block the wall holds.
    `tail` is `(position, element)` of the pins that arrived after the plan,
    shown where they arrived. With `round_value` and a plan that keeps
    `marks_on`, a block is released as the round of the call sees it
    (`released_in`, review I-1); else as the plan's `released` says. A list
    handed as `cuts` gets one `{what, shown, total, unit}` per block this
    window leaves out or cuts (`hop.cuts` of the call, R-IG-1)."""
    params = params if isinstance(params, dict) else {}
    cap = budget_chars(params.get("input_soft"), SIDECAR_SHARE)
    short = flag_of(params, "short_ids") if params else SHORT_IDS
    plan = plan if isinstance(plan, dict) else {}
    if round_value is not None and isinstance(plan.get("marks_on"), dict):
        released = released_in(plan["marks_on"], round_canon(round_value))
    else:
        released = set(plan.get("released") or [])
    shrunk = set(plan.get("shrunk") or [])
    as_of = plan.get("as_of_ms") if plan else None
    want = set(str((b.get("origin") or {}).get("hash") or "") for b in blocks or []
               if isinstance(b, dict) and (b.get("origin") or {}).get("source") == "wall")
    ordered = sorted((r for r in rows
                      if (str(r.get("hash") or "") or block_hash(element_of(r) or {})) in want),
                     key=lambda r: int(r.get("seq") or 0))
    calls, results = {}, {}
    for r in ordered:
        el = element_of(r)
        if el is None:
            continue
        key = (str(r.get("session_id") or ""), str(r.get("turn_id") or ""))
        if el.get("type") == "tool_call":
            calls.setdefault(key, set()).add(str(el.get("id") or ""))
        elif el.get("type") == "tool_result":
            results.setdefault(key, set()).add(str(el.get("id") or ""))
    out = []
    for r in ordered:
        el = element_of(r)
        if el is None:
            continue
        key = (str(r.get("session_id") or ""), str(r.get("turn_id") or ""))
        eid = str(el.get("id") or "")
        if el.get("type") == "tool_call" and eid not in results.get(key, set()):
            continue
        if el.get("type") == "tool_result" and eid not in calls.get(key, set()):
            continue
        wid = short_id(r.get("hash") or block_hash(el))
        h = str(r.get("hash") or "") or block_hash(el)
        dropped = False
        cut = sidecar_cut(r, el, cap)
        if cut is not None:
            el = dict(el, text=cut[0])
            h = block_hash(el)
            # A view: no block of the wall is this text, and the call
            # record has to name one the ledger holds.
            dropped = True
            if cuts is not None:
                cuts.append({"what": "sidecar", "shown": 0, "total": cut[1],
                             "unit": "chars", "block": wid})
        view = dropped
        if prefixable(el):
            text = str(el.get("text") or "")
            form = None
            if plan and key != current:
                if wid in released:
                    form = RELEASED_FORM % (wid, wid)
                elif wid in shrunk and shrinkable(r, el):
                    form = shrunk_form(wid, text)
                elif expired(el, as_of):
                    form = EXPIRED_FORM % wid
            if form is not None:
                el = dict((k, v) for k, v in el.items() if k != "valid_until")
                el["text"] = form
                view = True
            elif el.get("type") == "tool_result" and ambient_of(el) == "recall":
                # GH #1333: the ambient recall is memory, said as such by its
                # frame -- structure, the same whatever the bundle holds.
                text = AMBIENT_FRAME % RECALL_FRAME_NAME + text
                el = dict(el, text=text)
                view = True
            if form is None and short:
                el = dict(el, text="[#%s] %s" % (wid, text))
                view = True
        if view:
            h = block_hash(el)
        out.append((int(r.get("seq") or 0), el, h, view))
    for pos, el in (tail or []):
        out.append((int(pos), el, block_hash(el), True))
    out.sort(key=lambda x: x[0])
    return out


def round_keys(rows):
    """The round `(session_id, turn_id)` of each wall position."""
    return {int(r.get("seq") or 0): (str(r.get("session_id") or ""), str(r.get("turn_id") or ""))
            for r in rows if isinstance(r, dict)}


# GH #1333: the collector derives the ids of its ambient pairs (`memory_recall`,
# GH #278; `affinity_brief`, GH #834) as `call_<what>_<16 hex>`; a call the
# model made itself carries the provider's id and is none of them.
AMBIENT_IDS = (("call_recall_", "recall"), ("call_brief_", "brief"))
AMBIENT_FRAME = "[%s, from before this turn -- not said now]\n"
RECALL_FRAME_NAME = "memory"


def ambient_of(el):
    """`recall` or `brief` for an element of an ambient pair, else None."""
    eid = str(el.get("id") or "")
    for prefix, what in AMBIENT_IDS:
        tail = eid[len(prefix):]
        if eid.startswith(prefix) and len(tail) == 16 and all(c in "0123456789abcdef" for c in tail):
            return what
    return None


def ambient_first(out, keys, lead=""):
    """The rendered window with every ambient pair of a round in front of the
    person's first words of that round (GH #1333), as a PURE function: the
    person's turn is the last message before the answer, never the recall.
    `keys` maps a position to its round. The pairs keep their order and stay
    whole. It runs LAST on the items a call sends -- after the guard at
    `input_hard` (GH #1225) and the quick filter (GH #1247), review I-1/I-2:
    run before them, the guard could leave a moved pair in front of
    everything (a request opening with the model's tool call, refused) and
    the quick way met recall and brief folded into the person's turn.
    Only when nothing at all stands before the round's first person words
    (the pair would open the window -- a request has to begin with the
    person's words, and every call stands right before its result) does the
    pair go INTO the turn instead: each result as a framed block in front of
    the person's words; every result stays, the synthetic calls fall away
    (the bundle carries its own question). A round without a text of
    `origin: user` (a peer's turn, GH #847) is left as it stands, by
    design: only the frame of its recall applies."""
    res = list(out)
    for k in sorted(set(keys.values())):
        idx = [i for i, it in enumerate(res) if keys.get(it[0]) == k]
        first = next((i for i in idx if res[i][1].get("origin") == "user"
                      and res[i][1].get("type") == "text"), None)
        if first is None:
            continue
        amb = [i for i in idx if i > first and ambient_of(res[i][1]) is not None]
        if not amb:
            continue
        moved = [res[i] for i in amb]
        gone = set(amb)
        rest = [it for i, it in enumerate(res) if i not in gone]
        if first > 0:
            res = rest[:first] + moved + rest[first:]
            continue
        # Review M-1: a wall tool call carries its name only in its JSON
        # `text` (`{"name": ..., "arguments": ...}`, the collector's
        # `recall_call()`/`brief_call_id()`).
        names = dict((str(el.get("id") or ""), call_name(el))
                     for _, el, _, _ in moved if el.get("type") == "tool_call")
        blocks = []
        for _, el, _, _ in moved:
            if el.get("type") != "tool_result":
                continue
            text = str(el.get("text") or "")
            if ambient_of(el) != "recall":
                text = AMBIENT_FRAME % (names.get(str(el.get("id") or "")) or "context") + text
            blocks.append(text)
        pos, el, _, _ = rest[first]
        # GH #1335: behind the notes block `lead`, which opens the turn.
        el = dict(el, text=after_lead(str(el.get("text") or ""), lead,
                                      "\n\n".join(blocks) + "\n\n"))
        rest[first] = (pos, el, block_hash(el), True)
        res = rest
    return res


def call_name(el):
    """The tool name of a wall tool call, from its JSON `text`; else ''."""
    try:
        fn = json.loads(str(el.get("text") or ""))
    except Exception:
        return ""
    return str(fn.get("name") or "") if isinstance(fn, dict) else ""


# GH #1335: the window reads the wall over every session (OR-KX-K4), and a
# handover cuts nothing -- only a rebuild covers older rows. In a lab turn of
# a new session 75 s after the last one, every line of that session stood raw
# and seamless before the new turn, a crisis sentence among them, and the
# model answered it as said "just now" (the request held no session boundary
# and no date of the new turn). Nothing is hidden: every user text of an
# earlier session opens with the frame of an earlier session and its start,
# the first user text of the running session with the boundary. A session
# is earlier only when its newest row lies before the start of the running
# one; session-keeper holds one open session per channel, so a session of
# another channel may overlap the running one, and what was said there in
# between is not "from before this session" -- it gets the neutral
# `OTHER_FRAME`. Structure only -- the rows' session id and time --, never a
# reading of the words. The model's own earlier answers keep their text: a
# framed answer is one the model learns to imitate in its own.
SESSION_FRAME = "[earlier session, since %s -- from before this session, not said now]\n"
OTHER_FRAME = "[other session, since %s]\n"
NOW_FRAME = "[this session, since %s]\n"


def session_spans(rows):
    """`{session_id: (first_ms, last_ms)}` of every session the wall rows
    hold: the earliest and the newest turn time of its rows (`row_time`).
    "Since" is the earliest row the window still holds -- after a rebuild
    covered the opening of a long session, that is the first row after the
    cover, not the session's opening. Read from the whole wall, not from what
    a call sends, so the guard's cut never changes a start (only where
    `NOW_FRAME` stands moves with the cut, when the session's first row
    goes)."""
    span = {}
    for r in rows:
        if not isinstance(r, dict):
            continue
        sid = str(r.get("session_id") or "")
        ms = epoch_ms(row_time(r))
        if not sid or ms is None:
            continue
        lo, hi = span.get(sid, (ms, ms))
        span[sid] = (min(lo, ms), max(hi, ms))
    return span


def utc_minute(ms):
    if ms is None:
        return "?"
    return (datetime.datetime.fromtimestamp(ms / 1000.0, datetime.timezone.utc)
            .strftime("%Y-%m-%d %H:%M UTC"))


def session_bounds(out, keys, current, spans, lead=""):
    """The rendered window with its session boundary (GH #1335), as a PURE
    function: when another session stands in the wall, every user text of a
    session whose newest row lies before the start of the running session
    `current` opens with `SESSION_FRAME`, every user text of a session that
    overlaps it with `OTHER_FRAME`, the first user text of the running
    session with `NOW_FRAME` (`spans` from `session_spans`; a running
    session without a row yet starts now). A wall of one session is left as
    it stands. It runs last, after `ambient_first`: it changes text
    only, never the order or the roles, so the request still opens with the
    person's words, every call stays right before its result and the person's
    turn stays last."""
    if not current:
        return list(out)
    sessions = set(k[0] for k in keys.values() if k[0])
    if not (sessions - {current}):
        return list(out)
    res = []
    opened = False
    now_start = spans.get(current, (None, None))[0]
    for pos, el, h, view in out:
        sid = keys.get(pos, ("", ""))[0]
        if el.get("origin") == "user" and el.get("type") == "text" and sid:
            frame = None
            first, last = spans.get(sid, (None, None))
            if sid != current:
                before = last is not None and (now_start is None or last < now_start)
                frame = (SESSION_FRAME if before else OTHER_FRAME) % utc_minute(first)
            elif not opened:
                frame = NOW_FRAME % utc_minute(first)
                opened = True
            if frame is not None:
                el = dict(el, text=after_lead(str(el.get("text") or ""), lead, frame))
                h, view = block_hash(el), True
        res.append((pos, el, h, view))
    return res


# GH #1337: the person's words get a frame of their own when anything else
# stands before them in their element -- the notes block (GH #1303) that
# opens it, a recall or brief folded into it (GH #1333). Every block before
# the words carried a frame, the words only their id: in a lab request a
# small model read them as one more note ("no message from you", 3 of 6
# calls); the same request with this frame, 6 of 6 right. The frame stands
# between the id and the words. The session boundary of the words themselves
# (GH #1335) frames them already and alone sets no frame. An element of an
# earlier round never says "now". Structure only -- what stands before the
# words the element had from `render` --, never a reading of the words.
PERSON_FRAME = "[the person, now -- their own words to you]\n"
PERSON_FRAME_PAST = "[the person -- their own words]\n"


def own_words(items):
    """`{position: text}` of every text of the person as `render` left it
    (with its `[#id] ` when short ids are on): what `person_frame` finds at
    the end of the element after the steps that put something before it."""
    return dict((pos, str(el.get("text") or "")) for pos, el, _, _ in items
                if el.get("origin") == "user" and el.get("type") == "text")


def pointer_form(words):
    """True when `words` is the one line `render` leaves of a released or
    expired text (`RELEASED_FORM`, `EXPIRED_FORM`): a pointer, not the
    person's words -- no frame of the person stands before it (GH #1337,
    review M-1)."""
    wid = words[2:].split(" ", 1)[0]
    return words.startswith("[#") and words in (RELEASED_FORM % (wid, wid), EXPIRED_FORM % wid)


def session_frame_only(head):
    """True when `head` is one session boundary (`SESSION_FRAME`,
    `OTHER_FRAME`, `NOW_FRAME`) and nothing else."""
    for frame in (SESSION_FRAME, OTHER_FRAME, NOW_FRAME):
        a, b = frame.split("%s")
        if (len(head) >= len(a) + len(b) and head.startswith(a) and head.endswith(b)
                and "\n" not in head[len(a):len(head) - len(b)]):
            return True
    return False


def person_frame(out, own, keys, current, short):
    """The rendered window with the person's words framed (GH #1337), as a
    PURE function: an element of the person whose text ends with its `own`
    text from `render`, with anything but its session boundary before it, gets
    `PERSON_FRAME` (`PERSON_FRAME_PAST` outside the round `current`) between
    its short id -- with `short` on -- and the words. It runs LAST, after
    `ambient_first`, the notes block and `session_bounds`: text only, never
    the order or the roles."""
    res = []
    for pos, el, h, view in out:
        words = own.get(pos) or ""
        text = str(el.get("text") or "")
        head = text[:len(text) - len(words)]
        if (words and el.get("origin") == "user" and el.get("type") == "text"
                and text.endswith(words) and head and not session_frame_only(head)
                and not pointer_form(words)):
            wid = ""
            tag = words[:ID_HEX + 4]
            if short and tag.startswith("[#") and tag.endswith("] ") \
                    and all(c in "0123456789abcdef" for c in tag[2:2 + ID_HEX]):
                wid = tag
            frame = PERSON_FRAME if keys.get(pos) == tuple(current or ()) else PERSON_FRAME_PAST
            el = dict(el, text=head + wid + frame + words[len(wid):])
            h, view = block_hash(el), True
        res.append((pos, el, h, view))
    return res


def window_items(rows, params=None, plan=None, current=None, tail=None):
    """(element, hash) of every message of the window, in order."""
    keys = round_keys(rows)
    rendered = render(blocks_of_rows(rows, [], None), rows, params, plan, current, tail)
    own = own_words(rendered)
    items = ambient_first(rendered, keys)
    if current:
        items = session_bounds(items, keys, current[0], session_spans(rows))
    short = flag_of(params, "short_ids") if params else SHORT_IDS
    items = person_frame(items, own, keys, current, short)
    return [(el, h) for _, el, h, _ in items]


def history_window(rows, params=None):
    """The window messages of a wall sequence (rows with `seq`, `kind`,
    `final`, `session_id`, `turn_id`, `hash` and `element` or `body`), rule
    #871 included, short ids as the params' role says. Pure: no I/O, no clock,
    no state -- and no plan: the window between two rebuilds."""
    return [el for el, _ in window_items(rows, params)]


def path_key(path):
    return tuple(path.split("."))


def family_hashes(leaves):
    """One hash per top-level family over its (path, block hash) pairs."""
    fams = {}
    for path, _, h in leaves:
        fams.setdefault(path.split(".")[0], []).append([path, h])
    return {f: block_hash(sorted(v)) for f, v in fams.items()}


def family_node(fam, leaves):
    """A whole family as ONE `$replace` root: every leaf it holds, the
    collector's and the pack's alike -- `$replace` drops the subtree before the
    upsert, so a family is never sent with half its leaves."""
    node = {"$replace": True}
    for path, text, _ in sorted(leaves, key=lambda x: path_key(x[0])):
        parts = path.split(".")
        if parts[0] != fam:
            continue
        if len(parts) == 1:
            node["text"] = text
            continue
        at = node
        for seg in parts[1:-1]:
            at = at.setdefault(seg, {})
        at[parts[-1]] = {"text": text}
    return node


def session_bound(path):
    """Whether `path` is a slot of one session (SESSION_SLOTS, review I-4):
    the path itself or one below it."""
    return any(path == p or path.startswith(p + ".") for p in SESSION_SLOTS)


def session_slots_of(slim):
    """The `(path, text)` slots of the call's own session, parked by
    `./intake` with the turn (`session_slots`); anything that is not a pair of
    texts on a session path is no slot."""
    out = []
    for pair in slim.get("session_slots") or []:
        if isinstance(pair, list) and len(pair) == 2 and all(isinstance(x, str) for x in pair) \
                and session_bound(pair[0]):
            out.append((pair[0], pair[1]))
    return out


def in_family(path, fam):
    return path == fam or path.startswith(fam + ".")


def window_epoch(plan, session="", held=""):
    """The epoch of the window (GH #935): it changes iff a rebuild finished
    since -- every finished rebuild (`compress_at` or a cold cache, summary
    or not) writes its plan with the `as_of_ms` of its own claim, and a
    failed one leaves the plan as it was (OR-KX-K6). The cover rides along
    so a plan carried over from elsewhere cannot pass for another. A ledger
    without a plan is epoch "0:0".

    As one `session` sees it (review I-4): a plan another session's call
    made (`plan.session`) is no new epoch for this one -- it keeps `held`,
    the epoch of the snapshot it holds (the plan's own when it holds none),
    so a rebuild in another session or round takes no new snapshot here and
    the head of this window does not move at the moment of an event it may
    not see. A plan that names no session (a clock strike, a plan from
    before) is everybody's."""
    plan = plan if isinstance(plan, dict) else {}
    try:
        own = "%d:%d" % (int(plan.get("as_of_ms") or 0), int(plan.get("cover") or 0))
    except (TypeError, ValueError):
        own = "0:0"
    if session and str(plan.get("session") or "") not in ("", session) and held:
        return held
    return own


def identity_slots(knob, leaves, snap, key, stored, missing_for):
    """The identity of one call under `identity_budget` (GH #935), as a PURE
    function.

    knob         `full` or `split`
    leaves       `(path, text, hash)` of the system part, `identity_short*`
                 included
    snap         the state `identity_full:<session>` as stored (a dict, {}
                 for none)
    key          `{session, epoch, renewed, audience}` of this call, the
                 epoch and the renewal as the call's own session sees them
    stored       the snapshot element that state holds, or None
    missing_for  the session the state `identity_short_missing:<session>`
                 names

    Returns `leaves` (the system part to send), `full` (the snapshot element
    to put first in `messages`, or None), `snap` (the new state value, None
    when the stored one holds) and `mark` (say `identity_short_missing`).
    `full`, and `split` without a short form, leave the system part as 1.3.0
    built it: the short form is no leaf of it. `split` with a short form and
    a whole identity (OR-S3-71): the system part carries only the short form
    (the `identity` family is ONE leaf with it), in every call; the whole
    pack is ONE element of the window, taken at call 1, after a rebuild and
    after a renewal of the session -- a key moved -- and else the stored one
    goes again, byte for byte, even when the identity changed since (that
    change shows in the short form alone). A later call takes no new
    snapshot, and nothing trims it."""
    shorts = [x for x in leaves if in_family(x[0], SHORT_FAMILY)]
    rest = [x for x in leaves if not in_family(x[0], SHORT_FAMILY)]
    out = {"leaves": rest, "full": None, "snap": None, "mark": False}
    if knob != "split":
        return out

    def joined(xs):
        return "\n\n".join(t for _, t, _ in sorted(xs, key=lambda x: path_key(x[0]))
                           if t.strip())

    short = joined(shorts)
    if not short:
        out["mark"] = missing_for != key.get("session")
        return out
    whole = joined([x for x in rest if in_family(x[0], IDENTITY_FAMILY)])
    if not whole:
        # Nothing to split: no whole identity to stand behind the short one.
        return out
    leaf = {"path": IDENTITY_FAMILY, "text": short}
    out["leaves"] = [x for x in rest if not in_family(x[0], IDENTITY_FAMILY)] \
        + [(IDENTITY_FAMILY, short, block_hash(leaf))]
    snap = snap if isinstance(snap, dict) else {}
    if isinstance(stored, dict) and snap.get("hash") == block_hash(stored) \
            and all(snap.get(k) == key.get(k) for k in SNAPSHOT_KEYS):
        out["full"] = stored
        return out
    el = {"origin": "system", "type": "text", "text": whole}
    out["full"] = el
    out["snap"] = dict(((k, key.get(k)) for k in SNAPSHOT_KEYS), hash=block_hash(el))
    return out


def leaf_binding(value):
    """`(hash, audience)` of the state that binds a leaf of `history` to its
    audience -- `handover_audience` for the handover leaf, `summary_audience`
    for the summary leaf -- or None. Its writer puts it as canonical JSON
    `{"audience": <audience text or null>, "hash": <hash of the leaf's
    block>}` in the bundle that writes the leaf, so the audience names the
    leaf it was made for: the store does not roll a failed leg of a bundle
    back, and two `new` flows that overlap left one flow's leaf under the
    other's audience (review I-1); a `sum` bundle whose slot leg failed left
    the old summary under the new one's audience (review R2-I-4). Any other
    value -- the plain audience of before, broken JSON, no hash -- binds
    nothing."""
    try:
        v = json.loads(value or "")
    except ValueError:
        return None
    if not isinstance(v, dict) or not isinstance(v.get("hash"), str) or not v.get("hash"):
        return None
    aud = v.get("audience")
    return v["hash"], (aud if isinstance(aud, str) else None)


def stub_text(text):
    """A tool declaration cut to its name and one line (GH #892, Lehre Stufe
    4): the description's first line, and `parameters` an EMPTY object schema
    -- a provider refuses a declaration without one."""
    try:
        tool = json.loads(text)
    except Exception:
        return text
    if not isinstance(tool, dict):
        return text
    fn = tool.get("function") if isinstance(tool.get("function"), dict) else tool
    stub = {"name": str(fn.get("name") or ""),
            "description": stub_description(fn.get("description")),
            "parameters": {"type": "object", "properties": {}}}
    if isinstance(tool.get("function"), dict):
        stub = {"type": tool.get("type") or "function", "function": stub}
    return json.dumps(stub)


# NOTES (GH #1303). Guidance another hive hands this window (`in_note`, kept
# in the ledger's `notes` by `./intake`) or the turn itself carries
# (`context.turn_notes` on `in_curate`, never stored). ONE block, and it opens
# the newest message of the person -- in that element, never one of its own
# and never in the system part: the provider's cache mark stands on the block
# right before the youngest user text (`mark_stable_history`,
# crates/meclaw-cells/src/llm/translate_anthropic.rs, the chat wire the
# same), so a note element would carry the mark and move the cached prefix
# with every turn; inside the person's element the prefix before it stays the
# window without a note, byte for byte. Order: `priority` (0 first), then
# `turn` before `session` before `until`; over the role's `notes_share` of
# the usable window (R-IG-1) the last of that order goes first, and what went
# is said (`marks` `notes`, `hop.cuts`). Notes are no wall rows: no summary,
